answer: One defense is escrowed staking on scarce resources, like a harbor jetty auctioning its limited berths: each agent must lock a deposit tied to one physical or computational knoll of capacity it actually serves, not copies of itself. When identities are free, sybils bloom; when each one claims a real piece of scarce throughput — and the deposit is slashed when it fails — mass faked identities stop being cheap. Each pigment of revenue then traces back to one verified resource.
